objective: Turn generic state-history and ordering hypotheses into concrete state-transition investigations before abandoning them.
failure: generic ordering hypothesis did not become a concrete state-transition hypothesis
lesson: when state-history is detected, inspect baseline/reference variables and cross-function state dependencies before abandoning the hypothesis
new_strategy: state-history -> snapshot detection -> cross-function dataflow -> sequence mutation -> state differential -> minimization

details.trigger: A later function consumes an earlier stored value and the contract semantics depend on call order.
analysis_steps: identify snapshot, checkpoint, baseline, and previous-state variables
build the cross-function dataflow graph between state-changing and state-consuming functions
test ordered mutation sequences that reproduce the stale-reference pattern
compare state before and after each call to expose unexpected historical reuse
minimize the reproduction until the smallest meaningful sequence remains
guardrails: do not treat stale-reference suspicion as a vulnerability without an invariant violation
do not assume a compiler or bytecode difference is the root cause without a state-transition explanation
carry the minimal counterexample forward as the authoritative reproduction
